mainTopic: Whether vows affecting marital relations are עינוי נפש or דברים שבינו לבינה, and שמואל's rule on benefit vows, tested against the משנה about produce and a storekeeper.
overview: The גמרא finishes a proof from a משנה about a woman who vows 'I am removed from the Jews.' Her husband cancels only his own part, so such vows seem to be דברים שבינו לבינה and not עינוי נפש. The proof is limited: that משנה follows רבי יוסי, since רב הונא says the whole פרק is רבי יוסי. The extra mention of רבי יוסי's name in the משנה shows this, so for the רבנן the question remains. Next, שמואל, quoting לוי, rules that a husband can cancel 'benefit from so-and-so is forbidden to me' but not 'benefit from me is forbidden to so-and-so.' A משנה about 'produce of this country' seems to clash with this. רב יוסף answers that she said 'that you bring.' The גמרא tries the same answer for the storekeeper case, but the end of that משנה shows the vow must be broad. So the גמרא starts a fresh answer, and it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Proof from the woman who is removed from the Jews
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting a משנה: when a woman vows 'I am removed from the Jews,' the husband cancels only his part. It reasons that if this were an נדר עינוי נפש, he would cancel it for everyone. So such vows must be דברים שבינו לבינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He cancels his part, she may be with him, and she stays removed from all other Jews. If this were a vow of affliction, why would she stay removed from other Jews? Learn from this that it is a matter between him and her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a משנה and uses it to answer its open question: is a vow about intimacy an עינוי נפש vow or a matter between husband and wife?
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a husband cancels an עינוי נפש vow, the vow is cancelled completely, for everyone. Here the husband cancels only the part that affects him, and she stays forbidden to other men. That partial cancellation fits only a vow of type דברים שבינו לבינה.

keyTerms.meaning: He cancels his part, only the part of the vow that affects him
Removed from the Jews: she vowed not to be with any Jewish man
A vow of affliction, one that makes the wife suffer, which the husband may cancel
Matters between him and her, vows that harm the marriage itself
Learn from this: the formula for drawing a conclusion

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the husband cancels the vow completely here. He cancels only his own share, and that is exactly what makes it a proof.

phrases.english: he must nullify his part,
phrases.notes: This picks up partway through a משנה about a wife who vowed 'I am removed from the Jews.'

phrases.english: and she may be intimate with him,
but she remains removed from the Jews.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ נֶדֶר עִנּוּי נֶפֶשׁ הָוֵי,
phrases.english: And if you say it is a vow of affliction,
why should she remain removed from the Jews?
Learn from this
that they are matters between him and her.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ נֶדֶר עִנּוּי נֶפֶשׁ הָוֵי, אַמַּאי תְּהֵא נְטוּלָה מִן הַיְּהוּדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues an attempt, begun before this section, to settle whether intimacy vows are עינוי נפש or דברים שבינו לבינה.
steps.raayaObject: That vows affecting intimacy are דברים שבינו לבינה, not עינוי נפש.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה ruling that for 'נטולה אני מן היהודים' the husband cancels only his part.

steps.title: The proof only works for רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes the proof aside. The משנה of 'נטולה אני מן היהודים' follows רבי יוסי, so we still don't know what the רבנן hold.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the רבנן you still have the question, because 'I am removed from the Jews' is taught by רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits the proof. It works only for רבי יוסי's view, so the question stays open for the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof from step 1 is not wrong. It simply speaks for only one opinion. If that משנה reflects רבי יוסי, it tells us nothing about how the רבנן, who argue with him, classify these vows.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the רבנן, the Sages who argue with רבי יוסי
You still have the question; it is still unresolved
Teaches it, meaning he is the source of that ruling

phrases.english: According to the Rabbis, you still have the question,
because 'I am removed from the Jews'
is taught by Rabbi Yosei,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the proof of step 1 to רבי יוסי alone.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Partial: the proof stands for רבי יוסי but not for the רבנן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The source משנה reflects only רבי יוסי's opinion.

steps.title: רב הונא: the whole chapter is רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up its claim with רב הונא's statement that this entire פרק follows רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב הונא said: our whole chapter is רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for the claim in step 2 that the משנה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא makes a broad statement covering the whole פרק. Since the 'נטולה' משנה is part of this פרק, it must also be רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: Our whole chapter

phrases.english: As Rav Huna said:
Our entire chapter is Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא: כּוּלֵּיהּ פִּירְקִין רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הִיא
steps.raayaObject: That the 'נטולה אני מן היהודים' משנה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב הונא's statement that the whole פרק is רבי יוסי.

steps.title: How do we know the chapter is רבי יוסי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what basis רב הונא has for saying the whole chapter follows רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of רב הונא's claim. This sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Claiming that an entire פרק follows one תנא is a big claim. The גמרא wants evidence from the wording of the משנה itself.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? What is the source?

phrases.english: From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the basis of רב הונא's claim in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The textual source showing the chapter follows רבי יוסי.

steps.title: The repeated name of רבי יוסי shows the rest is his
steps.stepSummary: The משנה already said 'רבי יוסי says these are not vows of affliction.' So why does it repeat 'the words of רבי יוסי' later? This shows that from that point on, everything is רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the משנה teaches 'רבי יוסי says these are not vows of affliction,' why does it need to add again, 'He may nullify, the words of רבי יוסי'? Learn from this that from here onward it is all רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from the wording of the משנה: an extra mention of רבי יוסי's name signals that the rest of the משנה is his.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's view was already stated earlier, so naming him again seems unneeded. The גמרא reads the repetition as a marker: from here on, the משנה is speaking for רבי יוסי. That includes the 'נטולה' case.

keyTerms.meaning: To teach again, an extra teaching that seems unnecessary
From here onward

steps.whatToRemember: The 'נטולה אני מן היהודים' proof shows that רבי יוסי treats intimacy vows as דברים שבינו לבינה. For the רבנן, the question is still open.

phrases.english: Since it teaches:
Rabbi Yosei says
these are not vows of affliction,
why does it need to teach further
'He may nullify; the words of Rabbi Yosei'?
Learn from this:
from here onward it is Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּקָתָנֵי: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר אֵין אֵלּוּ נִדְרֵי עִינּוּי נֶפֶשׁ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The unneeded repetition of רבי יוסי's name shows that the rest of the משנה follows him.

steps.title: שמואל: vows the husband can and cannot cancel about benefit
steps.stepSummary: שמואל, quoting לוי, rules that a husband can cancel his wife's vows except 'benefit from me is forbidden to so-and-so.' He can cancel 'benefit from so-and-so is forbidden to me.'
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said in the name of לוי: a husband can cancel all vows of his wife except 'my benefit is forbidden to so-and-so,' which he cannot cancel. But 'benefit from so-and-so is forbidden to me,' he can cancel.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic opens. שמואל gives a rule about which benefit-vows a husband may cancel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she forbids someone else to benefit from her, she herself does not suffer, so he cannot cancel it. If she forbids herself to benefit from someone, she might need that person someday, so it counts as עינוי נפש and he can cancel it.

keyTerms.meaning: The husband cancels the vow
Benefit from me is forbidden to so-and-so
Benefit from so-and-so is forbidden to me
So-and-so, an unnamed person

steps.confusionAlert: The two phrases look almost the same. The key question is who is forbidden: others (he cannot cancel) or the wife herself (he can cancel).
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule for benefit-vows, and the next steps test it against a משנה.

phrases.english: Shmuel said in the name of Levi:
A husband can nullify all vows for his wife,
except for 'Benefit from me is forbidden to so-and-so,'
which he cannot nullify.
But 'Benefit from so-and-so is forbidden to me': he can nullify.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic after the רבי יוסי discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The husband can cancel 'הנאת פלוני עלי' but not 'הנאתי על פלוני'.

steps.title: Challenge from produce of this country
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says that if she forbids herself the produce of this country, he cannot cancel it, since he can bring her produce from another country. By the same logic, benefit from one person can be replaced by benefit from others, which seems to clash with שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: 'The produce of this country is forbidden to me': he can bring her produce from another country.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל with a משנה about a vow on a whole country's produce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats a replaceable item as no עינוי, because he can get it from somewhere else. Benefit from one person is also replaceable, since she can get help from others. So why does שמואל say he can cancel 'הנאת פלוני עלי'?

keyTerms.meaning: The produce of this country
Another country

phrases.english: We learned: 'The produce of this country is forbidden to me':
he can bring her produce from another country.
phrases.notes: In other words, she isn't really suffering, so he can't cancel this vow.

steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that 'הנאת פלוני עלי' can be cancelled.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a replaceable thing, like one country's produce, is not עינוי, then benefit from one replaceable person should not be עינוי either.

steps.title: רב יוסף: she said 'that you bring'
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that the משנה is about a woman who forbade only the produce her husband brings. Her vow is narrow, so it doesn't contradict שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: it is a case where she said, 'that you bring.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the challenge by narrowing the case in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She did not forbid the country's produce completely. She forbade only what her husband would bring her, and she can still get it in other ways. That limited vow is not עינוי, so the משנה says nothing against שמואל's ruling about a broader vow.

keyTerms.meaning: That she said, meaning the case is where she worded it this way
That you bring, limiting the vow to what the husband brings

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's rule stands. The 'produce of this country' משנה is about a narrow vow that covers only what the husband brings.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
It is where she said: 'that you bring.'
phrases.notes: She only forbade produce her husband would bring her, not the produce itself.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case in the משנה (אוקימתא).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say any replaceable item is not עינוי, which would clash with שמואל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a narrow vow limited to what the husband brings, so it does not clash with שמואל.

steps.title: A new challenge from the storekeeper case
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a husband cannot cancel his wife's vow forbidding a storekeeper's produce. This seems to contradict שמואל, who said he can cancel 'benefit from so-and-so is forbidden to me.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if she says 'the produce of this storekeeper is forbidden to me,' her husband cannot cancel the vow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the same משנה to challenge שמואל again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said a husband can cancel a vow like 'benefit from so-and-so is forbidden to me.' Forbidding one storekeeper's produce is a very similar kind of vow, yet the משנה says the husband cannot cancel it. So the משנה seems to argue with שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: storekeeper or shopkeeper
to cancel (a vow)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
"The produce of this storekeeper is forbidden to me"
phrases.notes: This is the very next line of the same משנה about produce of this country from Step 7.

phrases.english: he cannot cancel it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first challenge was answered, a second challenge is brought from the next clause of the same משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that a husband can cancel 'benefit from so-and-so is forbidden to me'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Forbidding one storekeeper's produce is like forbidding benefit from one person, yet the משנה says the husband cannot cancel it.

steps.title: Answer: she forbade only what her husband brings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with the same move as before: she forbade only the storekeeper's produce that her husband brings.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it is a case where she said: the produce that you bring from this storekeeper is forbidden to me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא borrows רב יוסף's answer from Step 8 and uses it on this line too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If her vow covers only what her husband brings, it is narrow. Other people can still supply her, so it does not cause her real suffering. This would not contradict שמואל, who spoke about a broad vow.

keyTerms.meaning: here too: the same answer applies
that you bring: her vow covers only what her husband brings

phrases.english: Here too
it is where she said "that you bring."
phrases.notes: She is talking to her husband: "the produce you bring me from this storekeeper."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 9 by using the same narrow-vow approach as Step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The vow covers all of the storekeeper's produce, which would clash with שמואל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The vow covers only what the husband brings, so it says nothing against שמואל.

steps.title: The end of the משנה doesn't fit that answer
steps.stepSummary: The משנה goes on: if this storekeeper is the husband's only source of food, he can cancel. If the vow were only about what he brings, why could he cancel? Someone else could bring it to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: If his food could come only from this storekeeper, he can cancel. But if she said 'what you bring,' why can he cancel?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 10 using the next clause of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the last clause the husband can cancel, which means the vow really makes her suffer. A vow limited to 'what you bring' would not cause suffering, because other people could bring her that storekeeper's produce. So the answer from Step 10 does not fit the end of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: his source of food or livelihood
why?
he can cancel

phrases.english: If his food could come only from him
he can cancel it.
And if you say that she said
"that you bring,"
why can he cancel?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ דְּקָא אָמְרָה שֶׁתָּבִיא אַתָּה אַמַּאי יָפֵר
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that her vow covered only what her husband brings
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's last clause lets him cancel, but a 'what you bring' vow causes no suffering, so that clause can't be talking about a 'what you bring' vow.

steps.title: So the first clause must also cover produce she brings
steps.stepSummary: Since the last clause must be about produce the husband does not bring, the first clause must also be about produce she brings herself. So the challenge to שמואל comes back.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, since the last clause is about what the husband does not bring, the first clause must be about what she herself brings!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its attack: both clauses deal with a broad vow, so the first clause still clashes with שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two clauses of the משנה describe the same vow, and they differ only in whether this storekeeper is the husband's only source. If the last clause covers even produce she brings, so does the first. In that broad case the husband cannot cancel, which goes back to clashing with שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: the last clause of a משנה
the first clause of a משנה
she brings

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question. It completes the attack from Step 11 and shows that the original challenge to שמואל is back.

phrases.english: Rather, since the last clause
is about what the husband does not bring,
the first clause is about what she brings!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מִדְּסֵיפָא דְּלָא מַיְיתֵי בַּעַל הָוֵי רֵישָׁא דְּקָא מַיְיתָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion of Step 11's challenge and brings back the challenge of Step 9.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reading the first clause in light of the last shows a broad vow that the husband cannot cancel, which goes against שמואל.

steps.title: A fresh start: the first clause really is a broad vow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops its earlier answer. It accepts that in the first clause the husband cannot cancel, even though the vow covers produce she brings herself. The reason comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: in the first clause he cannot cancel, and it is a case where she brings it herself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new approach. It admits the first clause is a broad vow, and the explanation of why it doesn't clash with שמואל continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of narrowing the vow, the גמרא now accepts that it is broad and that the husband still can't cancel it. That means there has to be a different reason this case is unlike שמואל's case. The גמרא gives that reason on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: rather: dropping the earlier answer and starting fresh

steps.whatToRemember: The 'what you bring' answer works for the produce-of-this-country case, but not for the storekeeper case. The גמרא now accepts a broad vow in the first clause and will need a new reason why it doesn't clash with שמואל.

phrases.english: Rather: in the first clause he cannot cancel,
and it is where she brings it herself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Drops the answer from Step 10 and starts a new way of answering the challenge in Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Retracting the earlier answer and accepting the broad case (setup for a new reason)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first clause could be narrowed to 'what you bring.'
steps.terutzMaskana: The first clause is a broad vow that the husband cannot cancel. The reason it doesn't clash with שמואל comes next.
